paper_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: What monomers and coupling method are used to synthesize the PNDIS-xBO random copolymers?
qa_pairs.answer: The PNDIS-xBO random copolymers are synthesized via Stille coupling polymerization. The process involves 2,5-bis(trimethylstannyl)-selenophene and two naphthalene diimide (NDI) monomers: NDI-DT (bearing 2-decyltetradecyl side chains) and NDI-BO (bearing 2-butyloctyl side chains).
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: What are the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and short-circuit current density (Jsc) of the optimized PSEHTT:PNDIS-30BO all-polymer solar cell?
qa_pairs.answer: The optimized all-polymer solar cell based on the PSEHTT:PNDIS-30BO blend achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 4.44% and a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 10.37 mA cm⁻².
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the increasing molar fraction of the 2-butyloctyl (BO) side chain influence the π–π stacking distance and crystalline domain size in PNDIS-xBO polymers?
qa_pairs.answer: Increasing the BO side chain content leads to closer molecular packing and larger crystals. Specifically, the π–π stacking distance decreases from 4.12 Å (0% BO) to 3.92 Å (50% BO), while the mean crystalline domain size (L) increases from 8.4 nm (0% BO) to 13.3 nm (50% BO).
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: Describe the specific device architecture used for the all-polymer solar cells in this research.
qa_pairs.answer: The study utilizes an inverted bulk heterojunction (BHJ) structure. The layers consist of ITO (indium tin oxide), followed by a ZnO electron-collecting layer, the polymer blend active layer, a MoO₃ hole-extracting layer, and finally a silver (Ag) electrode.
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the effect of treating the ZnO surface with ethanolamine on its work function and device performance?
qa_pairs.answer: Surface modification of the ZnO electrode with 1 vol% ethanolamine in 2-methoxyethanol reduces the ZnO work function from 4.4 eV to 3.9 eV. This improvement in the electronic interface results in enhanced performance for the solar cell devices.
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the solubility of PNDIS-50BO compare to other variants in the PNDIS-xBO series, and how does this affect processing?
qa_pairs.answer: While PNDIS, PNDIS-10BO, and PNDIS-30BO show excellent solubility (> 40 mg/mL) in chloroform and chlorobenzene, the solubility of PNDIS-50BO drops significantly to approximately 10 mg/mL. This limited solubility makes PNDIS-50BO more challenging to process in organic solvents.
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: Why does the use of PNDIS-xBO as an n-type material enhance the light harvesting of the solar cell when paired with the donor polymer PSEHTT?
qa_pairs.answer: External quantum efficiency (EQE) measurements show that PNDIS-xBO polymers exhibit a photoresponse in the 500–750 nm range. This is beneficial because the donor polymer PSEHTT does not absorb light beyond 700 nm, allowing the n-type polymer to contribute significantly to light harvesting in that spectral region.
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells

qa_pairs.question: How do the charge carrier mobilities of the PSEHTT:PNDIS-30BO blend compare to the reference PSEHTT:PNDIS system?
qa_pairs.answer: The PSEHTT:PNDIS-30BO blend system exhibits significantly higher charge transport, with an electron mobility of 6.5 × 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and a hole mobility of 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. These values are approximately 2.2 to 2.5 times higher than those measured in the reference PNDIS:PSEHTT blend.
qa_pairs.source_title: Side chain engineering of n-type conjugated polymer enhances photocurrent and efficiency of all-polymer solar cells
